A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with 14 complete, readable pages including Appendix A. Text extraction and visual comparison support reliable assessment of the figures, tables, equations, and proofs.

before.justification: v1 reports original Kinetics-600/400 evaluations, an airplane-rotation experiment, and GRW ablations (Figure 2 and Tables 1–5).

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark evaluations, airplane-rotation experiment, and ablation results reported in v1.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same frame-ordering contrastive objective, Gaussian acceleration prior, velocity regularization, and intermediate/final-layer applications. The model adaptations and training loss are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use Kinetics-600, Kinetics-400, and the airplane yaw/pitch/roll dataset. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Tables 1–5, including the MoViNet, MobileNetV3, X3D, transformer, VideoMamba, and attention-only comparisons in their corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: Section 4 retains the same training and evaluation settings, including 14 K600 fine-tuning epochs, 10 K400 epochs, single-clip evaluation, frame sampling, input resolutions, and accuracy/compute/memory metrics.

E4.justification: The airplane embedding analysis in Figure 2, placement and attention-head ablation in Table 4, and window/scaling/loss-weight sensitivity analyses in Table 5 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both Table 1 captions report three seeds and 78.4 ± 0.05 Top-1 accuracy, expressed as mean ± standard deviation, for MoViNet-A0-S-GRW. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative findings are retained. For example, MoViNet-A3-GRW remains at 85.6% Top-1 on K600 in Table 1 and 81.7% on K400 in Table 3.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation in Section 3 and Appendix A are identical. Theorem 1's O(T sqrt(ln T)) scaling bound, both supporting propositions, their assumptions, and their proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same smoothness-prior contribution, efficiency-constrained state-of-the-art claims, and reported 3.8%–6.4% K600 accuracy gains.

C2.justification: The explanations of temporal coherence and ablation outcomes remain unchanged, as do limitations concerning abrupt motion, untested large-capacity models, and frame-ordering complexity.

D1.justification: The abstract changes the code/model repository address from github.com/gilgoldm/grw-smoothing to github.com/cmusatyalab/grw-smoothing. This updates access information; implementation details remain unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish any change in repository contents or availability.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 32 references are unchanged. Positioning relative to efficient video architectures, slow feature analysis, and temporal-order learning remains identical.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 25 November 2025 to v2 dated 12 January 2026, alongside the repository-address edit. Narrative wording, terminology, and section structure are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: The updated repository address accompanies limited rewrapping of the abstract, and the margin stamp changes. Pages 2–14 render identically, with no changes to figures, tables, captions, or appendix layout.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, empirical evidence, interpretations, and appendix proofs are identical. The repository-address update and small first-page presentation changes do not establish a meaningful quality gain or loss; the PDFs provide no evidence that resource access has improved.
